title: School catering and food management: planning for next year
description: A practical guide for Kenyan school principals and bursars on planning food, managing the kitchen, and keeping quality up and wastage down.
body:
For boarding schools especially, food is the most visible daily service the school provides. It is also one of the most common sources of student complaints, and it is closely tied to student morale and the general calm of the school.

End-of-year is the right time to look at how the catering ran this year and plan how it should run next year.

Food quality affects the whole school climate

Persistent complaints about meals, left unaddressed, tend to build frustration that spills into other areas. Many schools find that fixing food problems early removes one of the most common grievances before it grows.

Plan menus around nutrition and cost

Work with the cook and a staff member responsible for catering to build a weekly menu that is balanced, varied, and within budget. Rotate dishes to avoid monotony. Where possible, buy staple foods in season and in bulk to lower costs, while planning storage carefully.

Create a student food committee: A small group of student representatives who meet the catering staff regularly to give feedback gives students a legitimate channel and gives the kitchen useful information. It is a low-cost way to reduce complaints.

Procure transparently

  • Get competitive quotes from several suppliers rather than relying on one.
  • Record what is delivered, in what quantity and quality, and who received it.
  • Review supplier performance each term and replace poor ones.
  • Store food properly to avoid spoilage and pest damage.

Hygiene is non-negotiable

Food handlers should have the required health checks, kitchens should be kept clean, and water should be safe. A single food safety incident can affect a large number of students at once.

Track cost per student per day

A simple record of food cost per learner per day tells you whether the catering budget is realistic, and where waste is happening. Review it each term and share the picture with the BOM.
